# Energy experiments (generated by tools/energy_experiments.py)

## 1. Ions stopping in a cold catcher, with a perfect laser

Fusion energy per unit of ion energy, for one ion fired into cold material (the best a laser could do is turn all its energy into ion energy).

| Ion energy | D into LiT | D into ⁶LiD | Li-6 into ⁶LiD |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 keV | 0.00011 | 2e-07 | 2.5e-19 |
| 100 keV | 0.0027 | 3.6e-06 | 1.1e-11 |
| 300 keV | 0.0037 | 3.6e-05 | 6.5e-08 |
| 1000 keV | 0.0024 | 0.00058 | 9.6e-06 |
| 3000 keV | 0.0044 | 0.0031 | 0.0001 |
| 10000 keV | 0.012 | 0.01 | 0.00048 |

Best ratio: D into LiT 0.021 at 20000 keV; D into LiD 0.017 at 20000 keV; Li into LiD 0.00084 at 20000 keV.

How much of a 6 fs pulse at the stripping threshold ends up as explosion energy (Coulomb energy / laser energy through the crystal): 10 nm crystal: 1%, 30 nm crystal: 4%, 100 nm crystal: 13%.

## 3. A ball packed with crystals, exploded at once

Energy in = explosion energy of every crystal + heating the electrons to 1 keV. Fusion out = fast ions slowing down + thermal burn until the ball flies apart, after subtracting X-ray (bremsstrahlung) losses. Best crystal size and fill for each fuel.

Two bounds for the fast-ion phase. *Generous*: the plasma is at its final temperature at once. *Conservative*: the ions slow down on the initial 1 keV electrons.

| Fuel | Bound | Crystal diameter | Fill | Plasma temperature | Fusion / X-ray power | Ball radius for breakeven | Fuel mass | Energy in at breakeven | Intensity to strip the crystals |

## 4. Proton–boron (p + ¹¹B → 3 α), the neutron-free fuel

Cross section: Nevins & Swain form as refitted in arXiv:2601.00241 (peak 1.08 b at 612 keV). Fuel: decaborane-11 (B₁₀H₁₄) crystals; catcher: cold decaborane.

| Crystal diameter | Fastest proton | Fusion energy / explosion energy (perfect laser, cold catcher) |
|---|---|---|
| 10 nm | 39.6 keV | 1.4e-13 |
| 30 nm | 356 keV | 3.2e-06 |
| 50 nm | 990 keV | 8.7e-05 |
| 100 nm | 3.96e+03 keV | 0.00021 |
| 200 nm | 1.58e+04 keV | 0.00023 |

Best single proton into cold decaborane: 0.0014 of its energy back as fusion.

**Avalanche test.** Can fusion alphas knock protons into further fusions, enough for a chain reaction (k ≥ 1)? k = secondary fusions per fusion; the nuclear boost multiplies the Rutherford elastic cross section, as an upper bound for nuclear scattering.

| Medium | k (Rutherford) | k (×5 nuclear boost) |
|---|---|---|
| cold solid decaborane | 7.4e-09 | 3.7e-08 |
| hot solid-density p-B plasma, T = 30 keV | 0.0008 | 0.004 |
| hot solid-density p-B plasma, T = 100 keV | 0.0032 | 0.016 |
| hot solid-density p-B plasma, T = 300 keV | 0.0034 | 0.017 |

A whole ball of exploded decaborane crystals is in the burn table of section 3 (fuel B10H14).

## 5. Electron screening ("lattice-enhanced" fusion)

Bound electrons in a solid lower the Coulomb barrier by a screening potential U_e (≈ 0.15 keV for atoms; up to ≈ 1 keV claimed in some metals). Deuterons into a cold tritide catcher:

| U_e | gain at 3 keV | at 30 keV | at 300 keV | best over all energies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 eV | 1.7e-11 | 0.00011 | 0.0037 | 0.00412 |
| 150 eV | 4.8e-11 | 0.00011 | 0.0037 | 0.00413 |
| 1000 eV | 3.6e-09 | 0.00014 | 0.0037 | 0.00416 |
| 3000 eV | 7.1e-07 | 0.00023 | 0.0037 | 0.00425 |

## 6. Check against a real experiment: the Texas Petawatt cluster-fusion record

Measured: 1.9×10⁷ neutrons per shot from 90–180 J, deuterium clusters, ion temperature kT = 18 keV (mean ion energy ≈ 14 keV), average atom density 10¹⁸–10¹⁹ cm⁻³, hot volume 1–10 mm³. Same model as the experimenters: Y = ½ n² ⟨σv⟩ V t, burn time t = plasma radius / mean ion speed, half of D+D reactions give a neutron.

| Density (cm⁻³) | Volume | Predicted neutrons | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1e+18 | 1 mm³ | 4.4e+05 | 1.9×10⁷ |
| 1e+18 | 10 mm³ | 9.4e+06 | 1.9×10⁷ |
| 3e+18 | 1 mm³ | 3.9e+06 | 1.9×10⁷ |
| 3e+18 | 10 mm³ | 8.5e+07 | 1.9×10⁷ |
| 1e+19 | 1 mm³ | 4.4e+07 | 1.9×10⁷ |
| 1e+19 | 10 mm³ | 9.4e+08 | 1.9×10⁷ |

A 14 keV mean ion energy corresponds to Coulomb-exploding clusters of 17 nm diameter in this model (the experimenters inferred clusters of roughly this size).
Measured fusion energy / laser energy: ≈ 2e-07, the same order as this project's estimates (10⁻⁸–10⁻⁷ for ions stopping in cold matter).

## 7. Exploding crystals as the ignition spark for compressed fuel (ion fast ignition)

The one published route by which laser-made ions could give net energy: compress D-T to ~400 g/cm³ with a main driver, then deliver ~10 kJ of ions into a ~20 µm spot within ~20 ps (Fernández et al., Nucl. Fusion 54, 054006). Designs of this type promise target gains ~100 (e.g. 250 kJ compression + 80–100 kJ ignitor). Can a layer of Coulomb-exploding LiD crystals be the ion source?

Deuteron stopping range in the compressed fuel (400 g/cm³, 5 keV): 2 MeV → 0.75 g/cm², 5 MeV → 1.3 g/cm², 10 MeV → 2 g/cm², 20 MeV → 2.9 g/cm², 40 MeV → 4.2 g/cm². A ~1.2 g/cm² range needs deuterons of about 4 MeV.

Crystal needed: about 117 nm diameter (stripping intensity 9e+20 W/cm²). Of its explosion energy, 13% is carried by deuterons in the useful band (within 25% of 4 MeV); laser → explosion energy efficiency ≈ 15%.

| Source distance from the 20 µm spot | Fraction of ions aimed at the spot (isotropic explosion) | Arrival spread of the useful deuterons | Ignitor laser energy for 10 kJ in the spot | Target gain (30 MJ yield ÷ 250 kJ compression + ignitor) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 µm | 0.026 | 0.23 ps | 2.1e+07 J | 1.4 |
| 100 µm | 0.0025 | 0.76 ps | 2.1e+08 J | 0.14 |
| 1000 µm | 2.5e-05 | 7.6 ps | 2.1e+10 J | 0.0014 |

An isotropic explosion sends almost all ions away from the spot: the spot covers only the solid-angle fraction (1 − cos θ)/2 of the sky seen from the crystals. Even with the crystals only 30 µm from the compressed core (not buildable: they would be swept into the imploding fuel and sit behind dense plasma the ignitor laser cannot cross), the ignitor needs ~20 MJ of laser and the target gain is ~1.4. At 0.1–1 mm it needs 0.2–20 GJ and the target loses energy. Fast-ignition designs instead assume directional, foil-accelerated ion beams with ~10% efficiency (~100 kJ of ignitor laser), and those are still undemonstrated. Shaped crystals are tested in tools/shaped_crystals.py.
